stances.summary: Warns of concentration risk and lack of diversification in AI sector
stances.quote:
As I'll get into in next week's free newsletter, circular financing is one part of a broader problem, that of concentration risk and the lack of diversification, especially at the top. 

www.wheresyoured.at/premium-the-...

stances.summary: Argues AI industry lacks real fundamentals; circular financing masks this
stances.quote:
This brings me to my final point. If AI was a real industry, this circular financing wouldn't be necessary. 

None of this is rational, or sensible, and circular financing only obfuscates the AI industry's real value. 

www.wheresyoured.at/premium-the-...

stances.summary: Opposes circular GPU financing arrangements and misleading profit reporting
stances.quote:
It shouldn't be legal for Coreweave to raise debt to buy NVIDIA GPUs on the back of an NVIDIA contract, and public companies shouldn't be able to report profits from paper gains in private companies as if they were publicly-traded. 

www.wheresyoured.at/premium-the-...

stances.summary: Calls for regulation of circular financing and stricter disclosure laws
stances.quote:
And just because something is legal doesn't mean it should be. Circular financing should be regulated out of existence, and we can start by reforming the law on financial disclosures. For example: every single customer above 4% of revenue must be named.
www.wheresyoured.at/premiu

stances.summary: Warns circular financing will collapse; criticizes as immoral despite legality
stances.quote:
To be clear, the circular financing we've seen is (most likely) legal, but it doesn't make it moral, and when it collapses there will be plenty of hurt to go around, with the warning signs blaring since 2023.

www.wheresyoured.at/premium-the-...

stances.summary: Distinguishes between legal circular financing and fraudulent bad faith operations
stances.quote:
You may wonder "how is this circular financing shit legal?" The (simplified) answer is that intent matters, and whether a company is operating in bad faith is what delineates stupidity from fraud. 

www.wheresyoured.at/premium-the-...

stances.summary: Compares current AI bubble to 1929 Wall Street speculation dynamics
stances.quote:
As an aside, there are a lot of troubling parallels between the current moment and the pre-1929 Wall Street. Like an ambivalence to company fundamentals, investors betting on vibes and buzz (with margin), and incestuous dealings.

www.wheresyoured.at/premium-the-...

stances.summary: Notes historical parallels to pre-1929 investment trust collapses
stances.quote:
That said, there are historical parallels from that era. Before the 1929 crash, Goldman Sachs operated a stack of self-feeling investment trusts, allowing gains and losses to circle and amplify. When it failed, it failed big. 

www.wheresyoured.at/premium-the-...

stances.summary: Argues AI circular financing is more incestuous and risky than historical precedents
stances.quote:
I have to be clear. Circular financing is distinct from, say, a corporate alliance, as I've seen argued. This isn't Dupont and GM in the early 1900s. The AI bubble is closer, more incestuous, and operates at an insane scale. 

www.wheresyoured.at/premium-the-...

stances.summary: Criticizes circular financing for replacing product focus with number manipulation
stances.quote:
Circular financing is catastrophic on a philosophical level for these companies, as it transforms their reasons for existing from "making products and services" to shuffling numbers around to create the illusion of success. 

www.wheresyoured.at/premium-the-...

stances.summary: Criticizes mainstream media for protecting power structures and repeating official narratives
stances.quote: Sadly there are large parts of the mainstream media that will coalesce to protect the system and repeat whatever the powerful says as gospel, and the only way to stop this from happening is to actually call them out by name again and again

stances.summary: Media failed to scrutinize AI, now seeking to cover consequences
stances.quote:
Though the media largely failed to scrutinize generative AI during its ascent, it now smells blood and is ready to pounce. The problem is, asking whether we're in an AI bubble doesn't really matter if we don't discuss the consequences.

www.wheresyoured.at/the-ai-hater...
